requirement: Also accept negative amounts written in accounting style, wrapped in parentheses: "($12.50)" is -1250. If s starts with "(" it must end with ")" (otherwise return the error "unbalanced parentheses", checked before anything else); the text between them is parsed as usual except that it may not start with "-" (that gives "missing $"), and the result is negated.
desc: Parse an amount like "$1,234.56" into cents. Format: an optional "-", then "$", then the dollars, then optionally a "." followed by exactly two digits of cents. The dollars are one or more decimal digits, either with no commas, or grouped as 1 to 3 digits followed by one or more groups of a comma and exactly 3 digits; ignoring commas, the dollars may not start with 0 unless they are exactly "0". Return dollars * 100 + cents, negated if there is a "-". A negative amount may instead be written in parentheses: if s starts with "(", it must end with ")" (otherwise the error is "unbalanced parentheses", checked before every other error); the text between the parentheses must then be "$", the dollars and optional cents as above (no "-"), and the result is negated. Errors, checked in this order: "missing $" if the character after the optional "-" (or after the "(") is not "$" (or there is none); "bad cents" if the amount contains a "." and the text after the first "." (up to the closing ")" if there is one) is not exactly two digits; "bad dollars" if the text between "$" and the first "." (or the end, or the closing ")") is not valid dollars.

decls.ts: type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: string };
